{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint PFS analysis not explicitly stated in Section 2.1.2",
      "quote": "The primary endpoint of Study 20190009 is progression-free Survival (PFS).",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "2.1.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The primary endpoint section describes the endpoint definition and estimand framework but does not state the specific statistical analysis method (e.g., Cox proportional hazards model) or how the hazard ratio will be estimated. The analysis is referenced to Section 9.4.2.2, but the primary endpoint section itself lacks a direct statement of the analysis.",
      "fix": "Add a sentence in Section 2.1.2 specifying the primary analysis method (e.g., stratified Cox regression) and the effect measure (hazard ratio) with confidence interval."
    },
    {
      "title": "Secondary endpoint DOR, TTR, DCR lack estimand attributes",
      "quote": "To compare efficacy of AMG 510 versus docetaxel as assessed by: duration of response (DOR), time to response (TTR), and disease control rate (DCR)",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "3",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The objectives/endpoints table lists DOR, TTR, and DCR as secondary endpoints, but no estimand attributes (target population, intercurrent events, summary measure) are provided for these endpoints, unlike the primary and key secondary endpoints. This is a gap in the estimand framework.",
      "fix": "Add estimand attributes for DOR, TTR, and DCR, including handling of intercurrent events (e.g., treatment discontinuation) and summary measures (e.g., hazard ratio, odds ratio)."
    },
    {
      "title": "PRO endpoint analysis missing for individual symptoms",
      "quote": "Change from baseline (cycle 1 day 1) over time to week 12 in disease related symptoms of: Dyspnea as measured by a 4-item dyspnea domain from QLQ-C30 and QLQ-LC13; Cough as measured by QLQ-LC13; Chest Pain as measured by QLQ-LC13",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "3",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The PRO endpoint is defined as change from baseline to week 12, but the analysis method (e.g., mixed model for repeated measures, analysis of covariance) is not stated in the endpoints table. The estimand description mentions 'change from baseline to Week 12' but not the statistical model or handling of missing data.",
      "fix": "Specify the statistical analysis method for PRO endpoints, including the model, covariates, and missing data handling (e.g., multiple imputation or mixed model repeated measures)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing data handling not described for primary endpoint",
      "quote": "Subjects who do not progress or die will be censored at their last evaluable disease assessment date.",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "2.1.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The primary endpoint definition includes censoring for subjects without events, but the protocol does not describe how missing disease assessments or other missing data (e.g., missed visits) are handled in the analysis. This is a gap in the statistical analysis plan.",
      "fix": "Add a description of missing data handling for PFS, such as sensitivity analyses for missing assessments or use of multiple imputation if appropriate."
    },
    {
      "title": "Multiplicity control not described for key secondary endpoints",
      "quote": "The key secondary endpoints are OS, objective response rate (ORR), patient-reported outcomes (PRO), including change from baseline (cycle 1 day 1) over time to week 12 in disease related symptoms (dyspnea, cough, and chest pain), physical functioning, and health related quality of life (QOL).",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "2.1.3",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The protocol lists multiple key secondary endpoints but does not describe how type I error will be controlled across these endpoints (e.g., hierarchical testing, alpha allocation). This is a critical gap for confirmatory trials.",
      "fix": "Add a section on multiplicity control for key secondary endpoints, specifying the testing hierarchy or alpha adjustment method."
    },
    {
      "title": "Sample size inputs not provided in extracted text",
      "quote": "The primary endpoint of Study 20190009 is progression-free Survival (PFS).",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "2.1.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The extracted text does not include any sample size section or inputs (e.g., assumed hazard ratio, event rate, power, alpha). Without this, the sample size justification is missing, which is a critical element of the statistical section.",
      "fix": "Include a sample size section with assumptions for PFS (e.g., median PFS in control, hazard ratio, accrual, follow-up) and the calculated number of events and subjects."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistency in PFS definition between sections",
      "quote": "Progression will be based on blinded independent central review (BICR) of disease response per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1 (RECIST v1.1).",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "3",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "In Section 2.1.2, PFS progression is based on 'independent radiologic assessment' while in Section 3 it is 'blinded independent central review (BICR)'. These are consistent in meaning but wording differs; ensure consistency to avoid ambiguity.",
      "fix": "Use the same term 'blinded independent central review (BICR)' in both sections."
    },
    {
      "title": "PRO estimand lacks handling of death as intercurrent event",
      "quote": "PRO measurements before or on start of new anti-cancer therapy including crossover will be used to estimate treatment effect.",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "3",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The PRO estimand addresses start of new anti-cancer therapy but does not mention how death (a common intercurrent event in advanced cancer) is handled. Death before week 12 would lead to missing PRO data, and the strategy is not specified.",
      "fix": "Add a strategy for death as an intercurrent event in the PRO estimand, such as using a composite strategy or treatment policy, and describe the corresponding analysis."
    }
  ]
}
